statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists in the current hour and Tail is held at the closed-venue floor, easing to 4% as the distance from the last verified kinetic step lengthens. Stress eases to 53%: a further hour has passed with no new verified action in the US-Iran tanker exchange, the IRGC counter-claim is still unconfirmed, and Friday's presidential characterisation of the conflict as "small potatoes" with "no fighting" sits against Iran's threat of more severe strikes. The scheduled 22:00 UTC Sunday reopen and the first full hour after it remain the two WATCH slots of this horizon.
recommendation: Tail holds a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant weekend hours and rises gradually to 14% in the final full hour of the halt, so the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green for the first twenty-one published hours. The 22:00 UTC reopening hour and the first full hour after it are each scored at 20% Tail and therefore map to WATCH and yellow; together they form the only published danger window. The last two slots step back to 17% and 15% and to green on the assumption of an orderly two-way auction. Stress runs from 53% down to a 52% low, rebuilds to 70% at the reopen and enters the high band from the fifteenth slot onward. Confidence declines from 85% to 73% as later slots rest on progressively older evidence.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 with roughly nineteen and a half hours of the CME weekend halt left; the Hormuz exchange stayed static for another hour and the 22:00 UTC reopen and the hour after it remain the horizon's only two WATCH slots
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, after ranging between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions inside that range, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. CME equity-index futures have been halted since the Friday 21:00 UTC settle and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September. That reopening hour and the first full hour after it are the two WATCH slots of this forecast; the horizon now extends one hour further into the new session than it did an hour ago.

The macro impulse into the halt is hawkish. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against roughly 56,000 expected, July was revised up to a 21,000 gain from a reported 23,000 decline, and the unemployment rate held at 4.1%. The 2-year yield rose about 5 basis points to 4.38% and the 10-year added a basis point to 4.776%; the Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 4 September carries 4.34% and 4.77% for 3 September, consistent with that move. Rate futures shifted to price roughly a 59% probability of a hike at the 15-16 September FOMC, up from about 55% before the release, and week-ahead commentary puts that figure near 57.5% against a current 3.50-3.75% target range. Equities absorbed the repricing calmly: the index held a small gain and VIX closed at 14.53 against a 14.32 previous close, having ranged only 13.80 to 14.58. A separate unresolved strand is the trade-embargo threat made late in Friday's session, which tied possible embargoes on deficit partners to a demand for lower policy rates.

The geopolitical sequence has not advanced kinetically in roughly twelve hours. US Central Command says American forces struck three Iranian crude oil tankers on Saturday morning, one of them near Kharg Island, after an aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer were targeted by ballistic missiles; two vessels were permanently disabled and a third destroyed, with no US servicemembers injured. Iran's military then warned that strikes on US vessels would be "more severe than before" if harassment of Iranian shipping and the naval blockade continue, and the IRGC claimed it had targeted three tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and three US-affiliated vessels elsewhere; that counter-claim remains unconfirmed and CENTCOM says neither US ship was hit. The latest live-blog entries add an Israeli assessment that Tehran is seeking to synchronise Hezbollah, Hamas and Houthi action, which is an intelligence assessment rather than a verified event. Pulling the other way, the US President described the conflict on Friday as "small potatoes" and said there is "no fighting" at present, and a 3 September assessment argued Iran and Hezbollah were unlikely to retaliate for the Ali al Taher clearance in the near term and might instead wait for a more advantageous moment to raise oil prices. The campaign therefore remains two-sided and unresolved rather than a confirmed escalation ladder, which is why Stress carries it and Tail does not.

Cross-asset context stays conflicted rather than aligned. WTI was last quoted near $91.48 and Brent near $96.28 after a weekly gain of roughly 9% for WTI and 7.6% for Brent, the strongest week since mid-July, an oil-led risk premium that pulls against equities. Friday's internals were rotational: every tracked semiconductor name rose, led by Micron and AMD, while five of eight megacaps fell, including Tesla at -5.92%, Apple and Microsoft, and delayed index futures closed split with NQ up 0.14% against ES down 0.42% and YM down 0.57%. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and belong in Stress, not in Tail.

The structural feature of this horizon is unchanged: roughly 49 hours of accumulated and so far unpriced information, an unresolved military exchange at a shipping chokepoint, an energy premium and untested hawkish rate pricing all meet a single opening auction rather than a continuous session. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so cash equities are closed and the futures session that follows the reopen is shortened, with equity-index matching halting around midday US central time and thinner order-book depth around any gap. That concentration is scored as a 20% Tail allowance in the 22:00 and 23:00 UTC slots, which maps to WATCH and yellow and forms the only published danger window, then steps down to 17% and 15% in the two hours after it. It is a conditional gap-and-extension allowance, not an assertion that directional structure has been observed: an orderly two-way auction with genuine retracement would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier of this sequence. Every earlier hour stays at or near the closed-venue floor and maps to EA_ON. The next seven-day calendar is led by PPI on Thursday 10 September and CPI on Friday 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, with the 15-16 September FOMC beyond this window.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 02:00 UTC on 5 September to 01:00 UTC on 6 September and lie entirely inside the CME weekend halt. All 24 slots are available from published Claude assessments, every one is scored at the closed-venue Tail floor of 5% under a normal mode, and every one maps to EA_ON and green. Stress was flat at 38% from 02:00 UTC through 10:00 UTC, climbed from 39% at 11:00 UTC to 42% by 14:00 UTC as the Saturday US-Iran sequence developed, stepped to 48% at 15:00 UTC once the CENTCOM tanker strikes were verified, rose to 52% by 19:00 UTC and peaked at 57% at 20:00 UTC when the Iranian counter-claim was published, then eased through 56% and 55% to 54% in the final two slots as that claim went unconfirmed. Confidence held in a narrow 85-86% band throughout, reflecting a complete evidence set in which only the live price path was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Twenty of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; the mapped policy state stays EA_ON with Tail on a 4-5% closed-venue floor through the dormant hours, lifting from 06:00 UTC as the Tel Aviv and Gulf Sunday cash sessions provide the first equity quotes since Friday and reaching 14% in the last full hour of the halt as a pre-auction gap allowance. The final four slots are different: futures are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on 6 September, so those hours are the first in which structure can exist. The reopening hour and the first full hour after it each carry a 20% Tail allowance, map to WATCH and yellow, and together form the only published danger window; the last two slots step back to 17% and 15% and to green on the assumption of an orderly auction. Stress opens at 53%, reaches a 52% low in the quietest overnight hours, rebuilds through the Sunday sessions to 70% at the reopen, then eases to 66%. The drivers are a two-sided and unconfirmed Hormuz tanker campaign that has now been static for roughly twelve hours, an oil complex up roughly 9% on the week, hawkish September rate pricing after the 162K August payroll print, and an unresolved trade-embargo threat, none of which has met an equity quote since Friday. The Labor Day holiday calendar implies a shortened Monday futures session and thinner depth around the reopen. Confidence declines from 85% to 73% because later slots rest on progressively older evidence during an actively developing sequence. Orderly two-way retracement at the reopen would decay both scores quickly, while repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the first genuine Tail amplifier.
